comment: Every AWS service the Terraform tree under infra/modules and infra/roots creates resources in, and the
Deny statements of each deployment role's policy that narrow what the role may do in it. This file is the
walks the tree, derives each resource type's service from its name, and requires the key set below to be
exactly the set of services it finds.
It exists because the fourth credentialed rehearsal (Actions run 35628963637, 21 September 2026) reported
25 errors in six classes, and every one of them was an action no offline layer in this repository had ever
compared with the Terraform it was meant to apply. The policy was prose in a runbook.
Until 27 September 2026 this file listed every resource type and the actions each needs: 47 entries and 562
lines, a second copy of the policy kept by hand. The list below is the same check at the granularity that
earns its keep. What it no longer catches: a lane that adds a resource type inside a service already named
here does not turn this red. The rehearsal's own deployment-role policy, which is the exact one production
gets, is what catches a missing action for it — one credentialed run, before production.
Each entry is per role, because the two differ: the rehearsal narrows its S3 and Secrets Manager reads with
carve-outs it needs for the Terraform backend and the RDS master secret, and production denies both outright.
An empty list is an assertion too: a Deny appearing over one of those services turns the check red until a
reviewer writes it down here. `unconditional_sids` is the other half of the review: every Allow the render
could not narrow, with the reason.

unconditional_sids.AccountMetadata: Read-only metadata. Describe, Get and List across the account, which is how Terraform refreshes state and how the release scripts read what they did not create; almost none of these APIs takes a resource, and the ones that do are read-only. No action here changes anything.
unconditional_sids.OriginAccessControlsCannotCarryATag: A CloudFront origin access control cannot be tagged and its id is assigned by AWS, so there is neither a name in the ARN nor a request tag to condition on. cloudfront:CreateOriginAccessControl under a RequestTag condition is what denied it on 21 September.
unconditional_sids.TaskDefinitionApisTakeNoResource: ecs:DeregisterTaskDefinition, ListTaskDefinitions and ListTaskDefinitionFamilies are documented with no resource-level permission. Registering is separately conditioned on aws:RequestTag/NamePrefix, and a task definition is inert until a service or a run-task names it, both of which are ARN-scoped, and until a task role is passed, which iam:* on role/<prefix>* is scoped by.
unconditional_sids.AdoptTheVpcDefaultSecurityGroupBeforeItC: The AWS provider revokes the rules on a new VPC's default security group before it tags it, so ec2:ResourceTag/NamePrefix cannot match at the moment of the revoke. The statement is narrowed instead to security groups that carry no NamePrefix tag at all, which excludes every group either environment has ever applied.
unconditional_sids.UseTheEnvironmentCertificate: acm:DescribeCertificate on every certificate in the account and region, because the exact ARN is a repository environment secret and shipping it here would put a value in the repository that the workflow deliberately keeps out. Read-only. Pass FSS_POLICY_CERTIFICATE_ARN to narrow it to the one ARN.
unconditional_sids.CompositeAlarmsAreEvaluatedAgainstEveryA: CloudWatch authorizes cloudwatch:PutCompositeAlarm against arn:aws:cloudwatch:<region>:<account>:alarm:* rather than against the composite alarm's own name, because the alarm rule references other alarms. David's simulation of 21 September showed exactly that: context.resource alarm:*, implicit deny, no matched statement, with the role's cloudwatch:* scoped to alarm:<prefix>*. A wildcard resource carries no tag either, so no tag condition can narrow this; the statement is the one action on alarm:*, and every other alarm action stays scoped by name.

action_groups.name: terraform backend: the S3 state object, its lock file and the DynamoDB lock item
action_groups.why: The release workflow's ambient credential is fss-rh-deploy and the S3 backend uses the ambient credential rather than the provider's assumed role. A production apply is local and its state is read by David's own admin principal, so fss-prod-deploy needs none of this.

action_groups.name: infra/scripts/rehearsal.sh guard: the leftovers reader
action_groups.why: The guard reads the run's state and then asks each service whether anything of the run survives it, which is the half of Appendix G 39 that a tag search alone cannot answer: an untagged leftover, a manual snapshot, an automated backup, a distribution, a log group, and the state lock the teardown may have left behind.

action_groups.name: infra/scripts/rehearsal.sh guard: the identity check and the read of everything tagged for the run
action_groups.why: The identity check and the production-inventory comparison, which are the two reads Appendix G 39 is measured with.

action_groups.name: infra/scripts/deploy.sh release and lib.sh: the one-off tasks and the two services
action_groups.why: fss migrate, fss admin database-users ensure and fss verify run as one-off ECS tasks inside the VPC, and the deploy scales the two services.

action_groups.name: infra/scripts/rehearsal.sh teardown: emptying the object-locked journal bucket
action_groups.why: GOVERNANCE object lock with a one-day retention means a same-day destroy has to bypass it, and terraform destroy cannot remove a bucket that still holds a version or a delete marker. Never on production: docs/greenfield/release.md 1.2.

action_groups.name: the release workflow's own two database entries
action_groups.why: A rehearsal is unattended, so it fills migration-database from the RDS-managed master secret and app-runtime-database from a password generated in the runner. In production David fills both by hand from stdin and the role is denied both actions.

action_groups.name: the smoke check's canary datapoint
action_groups.why: scripts/productionSmoke.mjs is handed CanaryCompletionAgeSeconds, which the workflow reads with cloudwatch get-metric-statistics.

denied_in_production.s3:BypassGovernanceRetention: The production suppression journal is an append-only record and Appendix E step 2 is a recovery. docs/greenfield/release.md 1.2.
denied_in_production.secretsmanager:PutSecretValue: David fills the eight production entries by hand from stdin. A deployment role that could write a value is a deployment role that could replace a signing key.
denied_in_production.secretsmanager:GetSecretValue: Nothing in a production apply reads a secret value. The migration credential is copied between two entries by David's own admin principal, not by the role.
